newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Liberty Mutual buys Brazil's Paulista Seguros.
newsitem.headline: Liberty Mutual buys Brazil's Paulista Seguros.

text.p: Liberty Mutual acquired a controlling 68 percent stake of Brazilian insurance firm Paulista Seguros in a $71.4 million deal, a Paulista spokesman said.

Liberty Mutual has also offered to buy the remaining 32 percent of Paulista from its 300 shareholders for $33.6 million, the spokesman said. The Finance Ministry's Susep department, responsible for regulating insurance firms, is expected to approve the deal in the next few days, he said.

Liberty Mutual plans to invest up to $150 million in Paulista Seguros, to reinforce the firm's presence in industrial and commercial risks and increase competitiveness in insurance for individuals. In addition, Liberty Mutual hopes to develop new market niches and attract its multinational clients to Brazil with the acquisition, he said.
"We expect to enter Brazil's work-related injury insurance market as soon as the government privatizes it," the spokesman said.
He said Liberty decided to invest in Brazil after the government implemented an anti-inflation plan and opened the economy to private investment.
"This created great growth prospects for the country's insurance market," he said.

The 90-year old Paulista Seguros is Brazil's seventh largest insurer, with business concentrated in the country's southern region. Last year, it posted premiums of 500 million reais ($487.9 million), of which 60 percent represented for insurance for individuals.
Liberty Mutual Group has assets totalling $37 billion and is one of the largest insurersin the United States.
